title: SLO Runway Insights & Priority Wave Tracker for Reliability OKRs
creator: Priya Kapoor
description:
Goal: Build a lightweight, opinionated ‘Runway Insights’ view and an associated Priority Wave Tracker to help PMs, SREs, and ENG triage services with shrinking error budgets and map remediation work to Reliability OKRs.

Why: Teams currently rely on raw SLI dashboards and ad-hoc Slack alerts. We need a single place that translates SLI burn into a short-term action plan: forecast runway, recommend priority waves (patch, infra, config, model fallback), and automatically create templated follow-up tickets when thresholds are crossed. This reduces time-to-action and improves consistent OKR alignment.

Scope:
- Runway Insights card per service + aggregated org view (24h/7d/30d forecasts).
- Burn-rate forecast engine (exponential smoothing) and confidence bands.
- Priority Wave suggestions with severity tags (P0/P1) and suggested owners.
- Auto-create follow-up Linear tickets with prefilled template when runway < 72h and burn sustained > 2x target.
- OKR linkage UI: mark waves against active Reliability OKRs and compute estimated effort vs OKR velocity.

Out of scope for this ticket: deep per-customer SLI slicing, long-term budgeting UI, and custom forecasting algorithms beyond the baseline model.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Runway Insights card shows accurate runway forecast for three sample services (ingest, runtime, routing) and aligns within 10% of simulation for past 30 days.
2) Priority Wave suggestions generated for simulated bursts and validated by SRE and Eng leads.
3) Auto-ticket generation creates PM- and ENG- friendly templates with links to implicated traces and dashboards.
4) OKR linkage can attach to an existing Reliability OKR and show estimated percent-of-OKR impact.

Success metrics:
- Mean time from threshold-crossing to assigned ticket < 30 minutes (automation enabled).
- Reduction of unplanned downtime incidents tied to SLO breaches by 15% during pilot.
- Teams adopt Priority Wave flow for at least 3 reliability incidents during the quarter.
acceptance_criteria: Runway card accuracy within 10% for 3 representative services (ingest, runtime, routing).
Priority Wave suggestions validated by SRE and Eng leads in pilot.
Auto-ticket creation with required fields (severity, suggested owner, repro links, dashboard snapshot).
OKR linkage displays percent-of-OKR impact and preserves lineage for reporting.
comments: 2026-02-25 - Kickoff: Scoped with SRE (Connor Nguyen) and Eng leads. Agreed to baseline forecasting algorithm (EWMA) for MVP to avoid overfitting.
2026-02-28 - Design sync: Aisha Patel (Design) provided initial mockups for Runway card and Priority Wave modal. Decision: keep visuals compact, use color-only severity with accessible patterns.
2026-03-03 - Engineering review: ENG-4829 will provide REST endpoint for daily rollups; ENG-4981 to add trace links in dashboard snapshots. Miguel to coordinate API contract.
2026-03-05 - PM review: Added acceptance criterion to ensure automation templates include mitigation steps and rollback notes. Agreed to default assignee pool = oncall rotation unless overridden.

2026-03-08 - Security: Security team flagged risk of auto-creating tickets with sensitive trace URLs. Action: sanitize prefilled payloads and require confirmation checkbox in ticket creation flow. Follow-up assigned to ENG-5012.

2026-03-10 - Prototype demo: Ran pilot on dev cluster for 'ingest' service. Forecast matched observed burn within 6% for the 7-day window. Feedback: add an 'explainability' tooltip for why a service was recommended into a Priority Wave.
tradeoffs_and_notes: Forecasting: Chose EWMA for MVP to minimize model ops burden; may underperform on highly bursty workloads. Plan to iterate if pilot shows systematic bias.
Automation vs noise: Conservative thresholds chosen (72h runway + sustained burn >2x) to limit false positives; may miss short severe spikes — will add a spike detector in a follow-up.
Granularity: Starting at service-level rather than customer-level to reduce data plumbing cost; per-customer slicing considered for next quarter if ROI is clear.
UI: Compact cards prioritized to keep Console pages readable; detailed modal contains links to full dashboards and traces.
